claims.text: A system prompt is a behaviour policy written as paragraphs, and it can be written as rows and as a JSON file a harness can check, with stronger controls in more places than the prompt.
claims.quote: Can it be represented as a behaviour policy?

claims.text: Anthropic publishes the system prompts for Claude's apps on a release notes page, with the note that they do not apply to the API; Claude Haiku 5.5's of 7 October 2026 was the one used.
claims.quote: These system prompt updates do not apply to the Claude API.

claims.text: OpenAI does not publish ChatGPT's prompt; the leaked file in the system_prompts_leaks collection, dated 22 August 2026, is unverified and used only as an illustration of shape.
claims.quote: I have no way to verify it, and I treat it as an illustration of shape, not as OpenAI's text.

claims.text: Haiku 5.5's prompt is 4,255 words and 181 sentences, of which 87 read as rules and 82 remain once five explanations are set aside.
claims.quote: I split it into 181 sentences and kept the 87 that read as rules

claims.text: The 82 rules sort into eight kinds: harm restriction 21, judgement 17, referral 13, conversation state 11, presentation 8, tool use 5, knowledge 5 and input trust 2.
claims.quote: Then I sorted the 82 by what kind of rule each is.

claims.text: The phrase for the rest of the conversation appears five times, and a refusal once made stands for the rest of the conversation.
claims.quote: stands for the rest of the conversation

claims.text: The prompt reads well as a policy, many rules carrying their reason, which is the why column, so the hypothesis holds: the prompt can be represented as rows.
claims.quote: The hypothesis holds: the prompt can be represented as rows.

claims.text: Five kinds, tool use, conversation state, referral, knowledge and input trust, could be held by the harness as a setting; together those are 36 of the 82 rules.
claims.quote: Together those are 36 of the 82 rules.

claims.text: Input trust is the strongest case: a sentence asking the model to doubt messages that claim to come from the vendor is exactly what a signature does better.
claims.quote: is exactly what a signature does better

claims.text: The 21 harm restrictions could be held in part by classifiers outside the model, as Anthropic's Constitutional Classifiers already do; the other 25, judgement and presentation, stay with the model.
claims.quote: That is a barrier around the model, not a sentence inside it.

value.unit: rules that stay with the model

claims.text: None of this says the prompt is wrong; a prompt cannot tell you which of its rules are kept only by the model, and a policy can.
claims.quote: a prompt cannot tell you which of its rules are only kept by the model, and a policy can

claims.text: The leaked ChatGPT prompt is about 18,000 words, and about six words in seven sit under its tool sections: its rules are mostly about reach.
claims.quote: about six words in seven sit under its tools

claims.text: A disabled tool and a sandbox without network are things the harness enforces; writing them into the prompt tells the model what the harness already does, but the rule's real home is not the text.
claims.quote: the rule's real home is not the text

claims.text: The two prompts are two halves of a behaviour policy, rules and reach; neither has a mandate, an authority order a harness can check, or a record of what keeps each rule.
claims.quote: So the two prompts are two halves of a behaviour policy.

claims.text: OpenAI's Model Spec has the best public answer to authority, a chain of command from root to guideline, and Anthropic's constitution separates hard constraints from defaults, but neither links a rule to its enforcement.
claims.quote: a root rule that is kept only by the model is still an expectation, however high its authority

claims.text: An ontology: one policy per layer, vendor, deployer and user, each with a mandate, a reach, its inputs and their trust, the state that changes rules mid-conversation, and rules with kind, trigger, decision, reason, authority, barrier, enforcement, tests and source text.
claims.quote: So here is the shape I propose, building on the columns this site's policies already use: mandate, reach, gap and barriers

claims.text: The taxonomy is the eight kinds, each with a natural home; the kind says where a rule could be kept, the barrier says where it is kept today, and the difference is the gap.
claims.quote: The kind says where a rule could be kept; the barrier says where it is kept today; the difference is the gap.

claims.text: The could_be field turns the policy into a plan for moving rules to a hook, a flag, a signature or a classifier, and a signed, versioned file makes a change to a vendor's rules a diff.
claims.quote: a change to a vendor's rules is a diff, not a re-read of four thousand words

claims.text: The formats are arriving: AGENTS.md, Claude Code's managed settings, AWS AgentCore Policy in Cedar, Microsoft's Agent Governance Toolkit, and OWASP's Agent Control Standard through hooks.
claims.quote: put allow, ask and deny rules in JSON that a user cannot override

claims.text: OWASP's list of risks for language model applications says the system prompt should not be considered a secret nor used as a security control.
claims.quote: the system prompt should not be considered a secret, nor should it be used as a security control

claims.text: No organisation was found publishing a written behaviour policy for an agent it runs; the closest is advice in Bloomberg Law that every consequential agent should operate under a written authority charter.
claims.quote: What I could not find is an organisation publishing a written behaviour policy for an agent it runs.

claims.text: The working examples known are on this site: the eleven-rule policy the session runs under, re-anchored after every summary, and the RiskMandate inbox team's.
claims.quote: the eleven-rule policy this session runs under

claims.text: The classification is the owner's, one reading of one prompt sentence by sentence; another reader would draw some lines differently.
claims.quote: One reading of one prompt, sentence by sentence; another reader would draw some lines differently.

claims.text: Could be kept is not is kept; what the harness or a classifier does today for each rule is not public beyond what Anthropic has published.
claims.quote: What the harness or a classifier does today for each rule is not public, beyond what Anthropic has published.

claims.text: The ChatGPT prompt is unverified, a leaked file used for its shape, and the six-in-seven figure is a count of words under its tool headings.
claims.quote: The ChatGPT prompt is unverified.

claims.text: The JSON shape is a proposal, not a standard, and not tested against a harness.
claims.quote: Not a standard, and not tested against a harness.

claims.text: The published prompts are for the apps; Anthropic says they do not apply to the API.
claims.quote: The published prompts are for the apps.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 14 October 2026; the analysis was done on the published Haiku 5.5 prompt fetched the same day, and a research agent gathered the formats and checked the quotes.
claims.quote: A research agent gathered the formats and examples, and the quotes were checked on the pages themselves.
